## 固定收益市場主線

9月18日，美國公債回吐週四的反彈漲幅。投資人預期聯準會將進一步升息，推高短期借貸成本；2年期殖利率上升9個基點至4.76%，10年期上升7個基點至5.01%。即使油價下跌、美國製造業產出意外萎縮，仍未能止住賣壓。通膨壓力不限於能源的新警訊、歐洲殖利率攀升，以及未來龐大的債券供給，共同壓抑債市。

市場已確信央行將採取行動，卻仍無法確定緊縮究竟要走多遠。美國長期通膨補償持平，實質殖利率則上升；日本如預期升息，但決策出現分歧，後續指引也不明確，令匯市失望。歐洲家庭通膨預期升高之際，法國主權債券風險溢價也擴大。信用市場仍能承接大型融資，但交易條件愈來愈能區分哪些借款人有穩定資金來源，哪些仍須仰賴出售資產或延後付款。

## 製造業產出轉弱，美債賣壓仍未消退

美國公債再度走跌，對聯準會下一步決策最敏感的天期領跌。5年期殖利率上升8個基點至4.86%，30年期上升5個基點至5.34%。2年與10年期利差收窄2個基點至25個基點，全週累計收窄8個基點。本月以來，2年期殖利率已上升57個基點，10年期上升30個基點，30年期則僅上升6個基點。

彭博對週五交易的報導指出，市場為建立空頭部位而借入近期發行2年與5年期公債的需求強勁，使持券人得以低於市場的利率融資。Mischler Financial Group的Tony Farren認為，這反映投資人預期聯準會首次升息後還會繼續升息。與此同時，多數歐洲公債市場殖利率也上揚，法國財政惡化更增添整體利率壓力。

美國抗通膨債券市場顯示，這波殖利率上升主要反映實質借貸成本提高。10年期TIPS殖利率上升7個基點至2.68%，同天期損益兩平通膨率則維持2.33%。固定收益市場收盤時，布蘭特原油期貨下跌0.91%至每桶$103.87，WTI下跌1.58%至$100.30。油價回落並未帶動名目或實質殖利率下降，而且布蘭特本月仍上漲14.12%。

堪薩斯市聯準銀行總裁Jeff Schmid週五表示支持本週升息，理由是物價壓力已遍及商品與服務，並非只是油價高漲所致。他認為經濟成長穩健、勞動市場均衡，關注的是通膨擴散的程度，而不是能源市場一天的漲跌。Schmid先前也曾表示，7月委員會決定維持利率不變時，他很可能就會支持升息。

不過，最新工廠數據削弱了從經濟活動面支持緊縮的理由。8月製造業產出下滑0.3%，不如預期的增加0.3%，結束連續七個月成長；7月增加0.2%的數字未修正。整體工業生產持平，低於市場預估的增加0.3%，也弱於7月的0.2%增幅。公用事業產出增加1.8%、採礦增加0.1%，抵銷了製造業的減幅。

耐久財製造業普遍轉弱，產出下滑0.5%，非耐久財則持平。汽車及零組件產出減少1.2%，商業設備減少0.5%，國防與太空設備減少1.2%，建築用品減少0.7%。電腦及周邊設備月減1.4%，但仍較去年同期高5.5%；半導體月減0.1%，年增率則仍達12.4%。科技產出雖仍有強勁年增幅，最近一個月的動能卻已轉弱。

整體工業生產仍較去年同期增加1.4%，製造業年增率則由1.2%降至0.9%。產能利用率維持76.3%，低於預估的76.4%，也比長期平均低3.1個百分點；製造業產能利用率下降0.3個百分點至75.7%，低於其平均值2.5個百分點。6月數據也遭下修，工業生產增幅由0.3%降至0.2%，製造業增幅由0.3%降至0.1%。世界大型企業研究會8月領先經濟指標下跌0.1%，不如預期的上升0.1%，前期則上升0.2%。

這些數據提供了動能放緩的具體證據，但抑制物價究竟需要多大緊縮力道，市場看法仍有分歧。美國銀行利率策略師Mark Cabana與Meghan Swiber週五警告，政策利率最終可能超過5%。其泰勒法則架構推算的利率約為5.3%；他們預估年底2年期美債殖利率將達5%，對10年期的外溢影響則有限，後者也將在5%左右。他們認為，官員會持續緊縮，直到認定金融情勢已具限制性。

這與該行經濟學家的預測不同：後者預期10月與12月各升息一次，2027年則維持政策不變。也有投資人認為，市場定價已過頭。WisdomTree的Kevin Flanagan認為短端可能超調，霸菱的Trevor Slaven則懷疑是否需要再升息三次。週末報導所述的期貨價格，已反映未來一年約80個基點的緊縮。在目前聯邦基金利率目標區間為3.75%至4%的情況下，爭論焦點是升息終點。

明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari週日延續了對通膨擴散的擔憂，除了受油價與關稅影響的品項，也明確點出服務價格。他在7月曾因主張當時就升息而投下異議票，並警告若等待過久，通膨可能根深柢固，屆時需要更強烈的行動。他也強調經濟韌性與勞動市場強勁，同時希望地緣衝突緩和能讓通膨重新下降。

相較之下，股市較美債平穩。標普500指數上漲0.17%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.67%，半導體股上漲2.78%，但標普多數成分股下跌。VIX降至14.81，季度衍生性商品到期帶動股票成交量異常放大。美元指數持平於100.22，黃金期貨上漲0.57%至每盎司$4,424.90。

## 日本升息，亞洲政策壓力各有不同

日本央行以7票對2票決議升息25個基點，將政策利率調至1.25%，日圓卻不升反貶。由首相高市早苗任命的Toichiro Asada與Ayano Sato均反對升息。由於本次升息幾乎已被市場完全預期，交易員要看的是央行對後續緊縮更明確的承諾，兩張反對票因而格外受到關注。

總裁植田和男表示，政策已進入必須防止通膨超過2%的階段，而不再只是確立通膨持續回到2%。他認為，及早行動可避免日後被迫快速升息；不排除10月再升息，也未排除未來某次採取更大幅度調整，但不願界定終點利率。本次距離前次升息僅三個月，是1990年以來日本央行兩次升息之間最短的間隔。

日圓盤中一度貶值1.3%至每美元158.05日圓，日本公債殖利率則各天期小幅下滑。富國銀行的Chidu Narayanan認為，植田談話中的鷹派內容不足以滿足市場期待。大和的Kento Minami同樣認為，異議票是偏鴿的意外，但央行對經濟與通膨的評估仍符合加快緊縮的方向。政策利率已進入央行估計中性區間的下緣，市場如何解讀未來的緊縮力道，也因此更為重要。

日經其後報導，日本央行曾向市場參與者詢問匯率水準，帶動日圓收復部分失地。紐約時間約下午1時20分，日圓貶幅縮至0.5%，報156.70。這項匯率詢價消息重新引發干預預期，日本財務省當時未能立即回應置評。今年夏季稍早，美日曾聯手支撐日圓，但週五的詢價報導並不能證明當天又有官方買進日圓。

日本8月各項通膨數據走勢不一，也使央行更難向市場說明本次決策。排除生鮮食品的消費者物價年增1.7%，低於前期的1.8%，經濟學家原預期持平；整體通膨與排除生鮮食品及能源的指標均為1.9%。以汽油補貼為主的政府支援措施，壓低整體通膨0.62個百分點，掩蓋了部分基礎物價壓力。

細項走勢並不一致。米價下跌15.7%，加工食品通膨由3%降至2.7%，但家庭耐久財、休閒相關耐久財與醫療費用漲幅加快。企業物價年增7.6%；帝國資料銀行統計，預定9月調漲價格的食品與飲料品項數，比一年前多83%。消費者端整體通膨雖然降溫，供應鏈上游仍承受相當大的價格壓力。

澳洲央行對通膨預期可能上移的風險說得更為明確。總裁Michele Bullock週五向國會議員表示，部分企業開始懷疑通膨是否會回到3%以下。她強調，這是逐漸浮現的疑慮，並非企業提出了明確、量化的預測。中東與天候衝擊持續，加上國內需求，使通膨與就業之間的取捨更加困難。

Bullock表示，儘管成長放緩，8月辨識的部分通膨上行風險仍正在實現，企業也正轉嫁較高的投入成本。若這些影響根植於薪資與定價，可能需要更強的政策回應。她作證後，市場隱含9月會議升息機率由約84%升至約90%，3年期公債也回吐部分稍早漲幅。目前政策利率為4.35%。

週日公布的Cotality初步住宅數據，則呈現國內需求的另一面。各州首府城市拍賣成交率下降4.6個百分點至54%；雖然當週拍賣住宅達1,832戶、較前週增加16%，但拍賣量已連續六週比去年同期少逾30%。雪梨成交率降至54%，墨爾本降至56%，顯示利率疑慮升高時，房市承接力也在轉弱。

中國週五公布的財政數據，則凸顯支撐內需的壓力。彭博依財政部數據計算，8月廣義政府支出年減6.7%，降幅大於7月的4.4%，廣義收入則年增2.9%。單月赤字縮減五分之一，前八個月累計赤字為人民幣5.5兆元。除了先前數據已顯示的放款減速，財政支持減弱也為內需疲軟提供了具體解釋。

官員正強調加速使用既有預算。政策性銀行已開始推動一項可帶動人民幣8,000億元資金的計畫，主要投入2026年基礎建設。中金公司苗延亮估計，今年剩餘期間已規劃但尚未發行的政府債券相當於GDP約1.1%，相關支出應足以協助達成4.5%至5%的成長目標。另在週日，市場監管機關承諾展開成本調查與價格檢查，以遏止破壞性的價格競爭。

印尼新任財長Suahasil Nazara確認，約印尼盾299兆元的政府備用資金將留在國營銀行至2027年7月，並透過每月與銀行及央行協調，避免日後提領造成資金缺口。他表示，8月赤字為GDP的0.93%，仍維持全年2.85%的目標，以及2027年擬議的2.4%目標。相較於先前承諾遵守法定3%上限，這次進一步交代了具體的流動性與財政安排。

## 歐洲通膨爭論升溫，主權評等分化

法國10年期公債相對德國的殖利率溢價週五擴大至103個基點，為14年來首次突破1個百分點。法國10年期殖利率約在4.50%，相對同天期利率交換的溢價達96個基點。歐洲債市普遍遭到拋售，但法國政府承認無法達成赤字目標，使法債另承受自身的財政壓力。

政府如今預估2026年赤字將達GDP的5.4%，高於財政法所訂的5%。總理Sebastien Lecornu提出總額€540億的措施以抑制支出，並在2027年將赤字降回5%。財長Roland Lescure週五為此目標辯護，也維持2029年降至歐盟3%上限的目標。然而，距離總統大選僅七個月，國會又高度分裂，法案能否通過仍充滿困難。

Scope將法國評等由AA-降至A+，展望穩定；Morningstar DBRS則維持AA評等，但將趨勢調為負向。Scope指出，法國財政一再偏離目標、債務增加、改革進展有限，並預期政治分裂將延續至大選之後。評等結果在當日利差擴大後才公布，進一步呼應市場對法國財政的擔憂。歐洲央行總裁拉加德表示，未見市場運作失序。

法國預算部週六進一步公布，預估2027年淨初級支出成長0.7%，低於歐盟執委會建議的1.2%上限。支出占GDP比率將由57.1%降至56.9%，稅收占比為44.2%；但債務占GDP比率仍將由2025年的115.7%、今年的119.3%，升至2027年的121.7%。即使落實擬議支出計畫，債務比率仍會攀升。完整提案預計9月底送交國會，歐盟執委會則於11月正式評估。

希臘的評等則獲調升。Scope將其調升至BBB+，是主要評等機構給予希臘的最高評等，也與Scope對義大利的評等相同。穆迪維持Baa3，但將展望改為正向。兩家機構肯定希臘持續維持初級財政盈餘、改善稅務行政，以及債務比率快速下降。希臘計畫於2026年提前償還約€130億紓困債務。Scope承認明年春季大選可能使組閣更複雜，但認為政策大幅逆轉的風險有限。

週五美國固定收益市場收盤後，穆迪將波蘭評等下調一級至A3，展望由負向改為穩定。穆迪批評，波蘭經濟成長高於趨勢、失業率低，又有大量歐盟資金，卻仍持續出現龐大赤字。華沙的預算草案預估2026年與2027年赤字均為GDP的7.1%，國防、醫療、社會支出與公共投資使支出居高不下。財長Andrzej Domanski承諾強化財政，但表示這需要包括總統在內的所有國家機構合作。

波蘭貨幣政策也出現新的鷹派訊號。貨幣政策委員Wieslaw Janczyk表示，若油氣成本加速上漲，可能有必要進一步緊縮，比總裁Adam Glapinski先前暗示維持利率至2027年中的立場更強硬。Janczyk認為，目前3.75%的利率具有緊縮效果，正實質利率有助抑制通膨，並表示寬鬆並不切實際。8月通膨為3.4%，接近2.5%目標上下各1個百分點容忍區間的上緣；他提出的條件式升息理由，部分取決於能源價格，以及政府限制燃料成本的措施。

歐洲央行方面，週五家庭調查顯示通膨預期進一步上升。消費者對未來一年通膨的預測，8月由2.9%升至3%；三年期由2.7%升至2.9%，五年期預期也上升。然而，受訪者仍預期未來一年經濟萎縮1.2%。物價預期升高，家庭對成長的預期卻未改善，讓政策更加棘手。

拉脫維亞央行總裁Martins Kazaks表示，若經濟活動依循歐洲央行基準情境，利率很可能走向具限制性的水準。他認為，成長愈強，進一步升息就愈容易，目前2.5%的存款利率並非上限。愛沙尼亞的Ulo Kaasik則強調預防的重要：第二輪效應尚未出現，但央行的職責就是避免其發生。

拉加德則更重視能源成本對整體經濟的影響。她週五強調，能源成本不會機械式地決定利率，因為也會影響成長與消費。義大利財長Giancarlo Giorgetti則反對以升息處理供給衝擊，指出緊縮本身無法化解供給驅動的通膨。彭博經濟學家調查目前預估，歐洲央行將於12月最後一次升息至2.75%，不再以9月為升息終點，並將此利率維持至2027年12月。市場定價更積極，預期至少還有三次升息。

希臘央行總裁Yannis Stournaras週六說明了10月與12月之間如何取捨。若9月通膨急升，或能源價格大幅走向歐洲央行的不利情境，可能有理由在10月升息；若仍有疑慮，則應等待下一輪預測，經濟活動轉弱也支持暫停。他目前尚未看到薪資驅動的第二輪效應，但指出在供給衝擊接連出現之餘，財政擴張與AI投資也帶來需求壓力。

雖然週五原油期貨下跌，實體能源供應消息仍足以讓央行保持警覺。沙烏地阿美通知至少兩家歐洲煉油商，10月將無法依長約供應原油，交付問題從先前9月的延誤進一步延伸。波蘭Orlen正尋找替代供應商；歐洲實體原油指標即期布蘭特原油價格當週曾突破每桶$130。法國總統馬克宏表示，將召集七大工業國討論再次釋出成品油儲備。

週末報導則點出運輸限制：以超大型油輪自休士頓運油至亞洲，成本約每桶$26，亦即每船$5,200萬，可能使長途替代供應失去經濟效益。沙烏地阿拉伯週六另表示，攔截了一枚射向利雅德的飛彈，並挫敗針對延布等民用設施的攻擊。局勢惡化之際，美國中央司令部則稱，荷莫茲海峽主要航道已無水雷，波斯灣盟友近幾個月經由海峽運出逾10億桶原油。卡達總理表示，華盛頓與德黑蘭之間仍有訊息往來。

英國方面，新增資訊在於英格蘭銀行已宣布的公債出售調整如何落實。巴克萊的Moyeen Islam認為，放慢縮表速度可減輕附買回融資工具的操作壓力，讓準備金更平緩地接近均衡。巴克萊統計，英格蘭銀行持有的2029年至2034年到期公債中，七檔有六檔的持有量占各券流通餘額30%至50%。可流通券源增加有限，可能使個別券種更難交易或借入；至於轉交債務管理局的債券將如何處理，仍待釐清。

## 融資管道仍暢通，借款成本卻更高

CleanSpark完成與Meta相關的資料中心融資，需求較交易啟動時明顯增強。這批5年期非投資等級債以面額98.5%的價格定價，殖利率8.25%，低於初步討論的約8.5%。發行規模擴大至近$22.8億，吸引約$100億訂單，超過發行額四倍；但殖利率仍比BB級債平均高約1.75個百分點。

這項計畫仍處施工階段，由Meta依20年租約保證支付租金與營運費用，最終定價確立了投資人願意接受的融資條件。雖然投資人接受了低於初步討論的殖利率，但相較今年稍早部分同樣以投資等級租戶支撐、殖利率低於6%的融資，借款成本仍高出許多。CoreWeave也完成$30億可轉債發行，但須提高票息、降低轉換溢價，才能吸引買方。

知情人士透露，軟銀有一系列規模更大的融資進展。以Arm股票質押的融資額度增加$50億至$250億，另一筆授信額度增加$4.5億至$65億，並取得用於OpenAI投資的$118.7億貸款。Apollo另正洽談將一筆貸款增加$36億至$90億。合計已承諾與仍在洽談的新增資金為$209.2億。

Arm擔保額度的利率仍為SOFR加約225個基點，再加25個基點的信用調整利差。軟銀原要求增額$30億至$50億，銀行願意提供約$70億，Arm今年股價上漲142%有助提高承作意願。截至5月，擔保品為7.69億股Arm股票，相當於這家晶片公司72%的股權。另一筆$65億額度由逾20家銀行參與，利率為SOFR加210個基點。上述利差均加計於浮動基準利率，並非固定的總借款利率。

軟銀本週也全數償還一年期OpenAI融資的$259億餘額，以較長天期借款取代短期負債。整體融資活動支應其對OpenAI的$650億投資承諾。熟悉投資人討論的人士表示，軟銀正考慮發行$100億至$200億債券；軟銀則稱紐約會議只是非交易性近況說明，尚未決定發債。儘管銀行對有擔保額度有承作興趣，軟銀CDS仍在本週稍早升至三年高點。

其他借款人也在規劃不同的市場融資途徑。摩根大通、桑坦德與NatWest為Drax收購Bluefield Solar Income Fund安排£11億過橋融資。銀行計畫今年稍晚或2027年初將債務分銷予機構投資人，也可能搭配Drax既有債務再融資。Drax正轉型朝靈活供電與儲能發展，這項收購將增添太陽能與風電資產。

韓美戰略投資公司已發出提案邀請，研議首次發行最高$20億美元債。該機構負責執行南韓對美國$3,500億投資承諾，可能於9月底前選定承銷安排銀行，明年初發行。目前融資討論仍屬初步階段；儘管媒體指首項計畫為德州燃氣電廠，政府表示尚未定案。

企業負債天期縮短，也已有研究提供整體量化證據。巴克萊週五指出，美國高評等債市平均到期年限已從高峰12.4年降至10.3年。歐洲今年約80%的發行在十年內到期，去年為65%。亞太企業在9月上半月僅發行一檔10年期以上（含10年期）、不可提前贖回的美元債，即農林中央金庫的$5億債券；2025年同期此類發行約為$67億。

縮短天期讓借款人不必將目前的利息成本鎖定太久，卻也使再融資更早到來。對保險公司與退休基金而言，除了大量AI相關發債，其他可供配置的長天期資產也更少。不過，初級市場整體融資仍暢通：美國投資等級債全週發行約$540億，歐洲則迎來4月以來債券發行最繁忙的週五。

基金流向較令人不安。LSEG Lipper數據顯示，全球債券基金淨申購降至$5.54億，為五個月來最低單週流入。短中期政府債與美國公債基金吸引$34.9億，連續第十一週淨流入；同類天期的投資等級債基金則流出$8.17億。投資人對政府債的需求，並未一致延伸至信用債與免稅債券。

截至週三的一週，市政債基金流出約$18億，為2025年4月以來最大撤資，也終結連續21週流入。贖回主要來自開放式基金，ETF也有資金流出。市政債今年報酬約為負1.7%，待價而沽、徵求買方報價的債券增至約$25億，同為2025年4月以來最高。週三10年期市政債殖利率約為同天期美債的74%。Hennion & Walsh的James Pruskowski警告，這類贖回循環很少一週就結束。

週五收盤，美國高收益債利差變動不大，強勢貨幣計價新興市場債利差則明顯收窄。不過，美債殖利率上升仍拖累報酬；經配息調整後，LQD下跌0.44%、HYG下跌0.24%、EMB下跌0.30%。

## 資產出售與再融資，決定信用表現分歧

Shapoorji Pallonji集團（SP集團）的債權人，一方面看見集團資產變現的前景改善，另一方面卻面臨近期償款可能延後的問題。集團正尋求將Porteast Investment零息債於9月30日應付的印度盧比350億元、約$3.65億款項，展延三至六個月。知情人士表示，7月籌得、原擬用於償付這筆債務的資金，正保留作其他用途。德意志銀行安排會議協商，債權人將獲得同意費，但條件仍在討論。

與此同時，SP集團旗下Mercury Finance的$6.5億美元債，票息14.5%，當週每美元面額上漲1.8美分，至創紀錄的101.9美分。塔塔集團控股公司Tata Sons決定推動上市，可能讓SP持有的18.4%股權價值得以實現，因而帶動投資人買進。部分Eqyizen盧比債以18.75%殖利率向投資人報價，低於7月發行時的18.95%；部分分銷商也將最低認購額由印度盧比1億元降至1,000萬元。

持股未來可能變現，仍無法解決Porteast眼前的付款問題。其去年以19.75%年殖利率籌得的$34億零息融資，以塔塔持股擔保；允許貸款成數上限由34%提高至40%的豁免，先前已展延至9月30日。週末，Tata Trusts對N. Chandrasekaran續任Tata Sons董事長決議的法律效力提出異議，雙方聘請律師，可能展開長期爭訟，也使投資人寄望持股變現的前景多了公司治理變數。

巴西鋼鐵公司CSN的資產出售則有更具體進展。熟悉協商的人士表示，Huaxin、Votorantim與Polimix各就其水泥事業提出約巴西雷亞爾110億元的具約束力報價，低於公司要求的150億元，但CSN可能接受較低價格。該事業已作為至少$12億貸款的擔保，因此如何處理質押資產，將影響出售所得可用於降債的金額。

CSN另正出售德國Stahlwerk Thuringen，並考慮分別出售基礎建設資產，而不是整批出售少數股權。自Fabio Schvartsman於9月2日出任執行長後，公司債券報酬約5%，同期廣泛新興市場企業債指標下跌0.5%；即使反彈，今年報酬仍約為負11.2%。公司已連續十季淨損，6月30日淨負債為巴西雷亞爾421億元，相當於EBITDA的3.5倍。資產負債表壓力究竟能緩解多少，如今取決於出售交易能否落實，而不只是管理層更替。

歐洲房地產債則出現融資受挫的案例。Net Zero Properties（NZP）即使提供發行折價並提高票息，仍放棄€5億發債。其6月利息保障倍數為1.3倍，已接近中期政策下限1.2倍。部分募資原擬用於償還成本更高的Castlelake夾層債務，但投資人質疑付息後的現金創造能力，以及房地產組合估值。

NZP表示，訂單已足額覆蓋發行規模，只因市場波動使定價高於其他較便宜的融資選項而取消，並稱有充足資金進行收購。當時房地產已是歐洲高收益債當月表現最弱的產業，報酬負2.03%，整體指數則為負0.9%。Vivion票息8.125%的混合資本債，交易價格約為面額的85%。融資成本升高同時壓迫償債能力與房產估值，租金卻調整較慢。

另一篇週末調查報導指出歐洲房地產放款的不同風險。監管機關加強檢視火災、洪水與乾旱曝險之際，銀行表示，隱私限制使其難以取得借款人的保險及建築物狀況資料。歐洲央行特別指出，保險每年續約，但貸款可能長達30年，兩者期限並不相稱。裕信銀行已增提€1億氣候相關準備。問題在於，承作貸款時保障擔保品的保險，日後是否仍能買到、保費是否仍可負擔。

主權信用方面，穆迪週五稍晚將莫三比克降至Caa3，警告國內融資壓力已蔓延至外部債務。莫三比克的$9億2031年到期歐洲債券仍正常履約，但該評等對應的是可能使投資人損失20%至35%的重整情境。2025年底，外部欠款已達$3.28億。這次降評對債券先前回升所反映的樂觀構成挑戰；債券價格已漲至面額94.88%，比4月低點高近30%。

國際貨幣基金（IMF）訪問團週五結束任務，指出當地經濟活動低迷，但已有復甦跡象。莫三比克政府表示，11月訪問可能促成工作層級協議。即使大型液化天然氣計畫持續推進，援助計畫協商與債務處理方式仍未定案；穆迪提出的損失區間是其對重整的評估，並非債權人已同意的條件。

巴基斯坦則傳出融資改善。總理辦公室表示，歐洲債券募資款到位後，外匯存底達創紀錄的$214億，並提到匯款、服務出口與經常帳均有改善。新資金增強了對外支付緩衝，但對進口能源的依賴仍是弱點。近期發債擴大了融資選項，IMF預計也將於未來一週到訪。

新興市場最新配置資料顯示，投資人較偏好當地貨幣債，而非美元債。美國銀行9月4日至9日調查38位管理合計$4,440億資產的經理人，其中84%相對強勢貨幣債加碼當地貨幣債，8月僅38%。自6月底以來，當地貨幣主權債表現優於美元債逾3個百分點。9月以來，規模最大的美元債ETF流出逾$8億，最大的當地貨幣債ETF則吸引約$4,100萬。

不過，美元仍限制這項配置偏好。上週美元普遍走強之際，新興市場當地貨幣債報酬與美元的負相關程度也加深。Robeco的Diliana Deltcheva認為，當地市場機會較多，美元債進一步收窄利差的空間有限；Jupiter的Harry Richards則警告，美債殖利率升高，對較弱發行人的再融資能力尤其不利。當地貨幣債能否繼續領先，除了起始殖利率，也取決於各國通膨與匯率走勢。

## 後續市場觀察

9月22日的$690億2年期美債標售，以及9月23日的$700億5年期標售，將檢驗領跌天期的市場需求，9月24日接著有7年期標售。Mischler的Tony Farren指出，下週美國公債標售總額逾$7,000億，交易商另預期約$400億美國高評等企業債發行。Sysco可能為收購Jetro Restaurant Depot籌資$170億，包括30年與40年期債券；軟銀若發債，也將另行吸收大量資金。

製造業萎縮後，後續成長數據更為關鍵。9月22日將公布ADP每週就業估計與里奇蒙聯準銀行調查，9月23日則有標普全球9月PMI初值。市場預估製造業由53.9降至53.6，服務業由56.5降至56。9月24日失業救濟申請，以及9月25日耐久財與資本財數據，將有助判斷8月產出轉弱是否擴散至就業與投資。週五密西根大學調查終值也將更新通膨預期。

市場預期的後續緊縮幅度已明顯高於決策官員預測的中位數，聯準會接下來的溝通將回應這項落差。Austan Goolsbee週一發言，John Williams與Philip Jefferson列入週二講者，Beth Hammack則於週四發言。重要的是，官員會將工廠產出轉弱視為緊縮逐漸奏效，還是如Schmid與Kashkari一樣，繼續強調通膨廣泛與需求韌性。

Scott Bessent與何立峰已在紐約展開貿易談判，之後是9月24日川習峰會。議程包括延長11月到期的貿易休戰、關稅、投資與AI。相較先前美國延後宣布關稅，任何休戰展延的期間與條件更加重要，因為這將決定會後還剩多少貿易成本再度上升的不確定性。

週五傳出匯率詢價後，日本假期持續至週三，增加匯率劇烈波動的風險。流動性偏低可能放大日圓再次走弱的幅度，也可能放大官方行動的市場影響。沙烏地取消10月供油配額後，能源市場則面臨實際交付考驗：替代供應、運費與紅海周邊基礎設施安全，將決定期貨價格下降能否真正減輕煉油商成本。

印度預計9月25日敲定10月至次年3月的舉債日程，規劃總發行額印度盧比7.96兆元，其中包括9月11日3年期標售失敗、未能籌得的650億元。市場參與者偏好增加3年與5年期供給，但印度央行為回收流動性而出售債券，已對短端利率造成上行壓力。摩根大通的Jahangir Aziz週五另警告，儘管預期首次升息25個基點，市場可能高估先前刺激措施退場後仍能維持的緊縮幅度。因此，發債天期配置將面對仍不明朗的政策前景。

日本升息25個基點至1.25%，但表決分歧、後續指引不明確，使日圓走弱；其後傳出匯率詢價，日圓才收復部分跌幅。法國政府承認赤字將高於預期，10年期公債相對德國的殖利率溢價擴大至103個基點，同時歐洲家庭通膨預期上升。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries surrendered Thursday's relief rally on September 18 as investors pushed short-term borrowing costs higher in anticipation of further Federal Reserve tightening. The 2-year yield rose 9 basis points to 4.76%, and the 10-year climbed 7 basis points to 5.01%. Falling oil prices and an unexpected contraction in U.S. factory production failed to arrest the selling. Fresh warnings about inflation beyond energy, rising European yields and heavy prospective debt supply kept the pressure on bonds.

The day's distinction was between confidence that central banks would act and uncertainty over how far they would have to go. Long-term U.S. inflation compensation held steady while real yields rose. Japan delivered its expected rate increase but disappointed currency markets with a divided vote and inconclusive guidance. In Europe, higher household inflation expectations accompanied a widening French sovereign premium. Credit markets remained open to large financings, but the terms increasingly separated borrowers with dependable funding access from those relying on asset sales or payment extensions.

## Treasury Selling Persists Despite Weaker Factory Output

The renewed Treasury decline was led by the maturities most sensitive to the Fed's next decisions. The 5-year yield rose 8 basis points to 4.86%, while the 30-year increased 5 basis points to 5.34%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 2 basis points to 25, taking its weekly flattening to 8 basis points. Over the month, the 2-year yield had risen 57 basis points, compared with 30 for the 10-year and just 6 for the 30-year.

Demand to borrow recently issued 2- and 5-year notes for short positions was sufficiently strong that holders could finance them at below-market rates, according to Bloomberg's account of Friday trading. Mischler Financial Group's Tony Farren attributed that demand to expectations that the Fed's first increase would be followed by others. The selling also coincided with higher yields across most European government markets, where France's fiscal deterioration added to the broader rate pressure.

The U.S. inflation-linked market again located the immediate adjustment in real borrowing costs. The 10-year TIPS yield rose 7 basis points to 2.68%, while the corresponding breakeven held at 2.33%. Brent futures fell 0.91% to $103.87 a barrel and WTI declined 1.58% to $100.30 at the fixed-income close. Lower crude therefore did not translate into lower nominal or real yields, although Brent remained 14.12% higher over the month.

Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid supplied an independent policy signal on Friday, supporting this week's increase because price pressure was extending across goods and services, not merely reflecting expensive oil. He described economic growth as solid and the labor market as balanced. His assessment placed the emphasis on the breadth of inflation rather than a daily change in the energy market. Schmid had previously said he probably would have supported an increase in July, when the committee held rates steady.

The new factory figures nevertheless weakened the activity side of the argument. August manufacturing production fell 0.3%, against expectations for a 0.3% increase, ending seven consecutive monthly gains. July's 0.2% increase was unrevised. Overall industrial production was unchanged, below the 0.3% consensus and following July's 0.2% gain, with a 1.8% increase in utilities and a 0.1% rise in mining offsetting the manufacturing decline.

Weakness was spread across durable manufacturing, where output fell 0.5%; nondurable production was unchanged. Motor vehicles and parts declined 1.2%, business equipment fell 0.5%, defense and space equipment dropped 1.2%, and construction supplies decreased 0.7%. Computer and peripheral-equipment output fell 1.4% on the month, although it remained 5.5% above a year earlier. Semiconductor production slipped 0.1% but was still 12.4% higher year over year. Strong annual technology comparisons thus coexisted with a weaker latest month.

Total industrial production remained 1.4% above a year earlier, while manufacturing's annual gain slowed to 0.9% from 1.2%. Capacity utilization held at 76.3%, below the 76.4% consensus and 3.1 percentage points beneath its long-run average. Manufacturing utilization fell 0.3 percentage point to 75.7%, or 2.5 points below its average. Revisions also trimmed June's industrial-production growth to 0.2% from 0.3% and manufacturing growth to 0.1% from 0.3%. The Conference Board's August Leading Economic Index fell 0.1%, against expectations for a 0.1% increase and a previous 0.2% rise.

Those releases provided concrete evidence of softer momentum, but investors still faced disagreement over the restraint needed to contain prices. Bank of America rates strategists Mark Cabana and Meghan Swiber warned Friday that the policy rate could ultimately exceed 5%. Their Taylor-rule framework implied roughly 5.3%, and they projected a 5% 2-year Treasury yield at year-end while expecting limited spillover to a 10-year yield also near 5%. Their interpretation was that officials would continue tightening until they regarded financial conditions as restrictive.

That was distinct from the bank's economists' forecast of increases in October and December followed by no policy change in 2027. Other investors thought market pricing had already gone too far. WisdomTree's Kevin Flanagan saw a potential overshoot at the front end; Barings' Trevor Slaven doubted that three additional increases would be needed. Futures pricing described in weekend reporting incorporated about 80 basis points of tightening over the coming year. The disagreement was about the endpoint, with the current federal funds target at 3.75%-4%.

On Sunday, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari reinforced the concern about inflation breadth, explicitly identifying services as well as categories affected by oil and tariffs. A July dissenter who had preferred an increase then, Kashkari warned that waiting too long could allow inflation to become entrenched and require stronger action. He also emphasized economic resilience and a strong labor market, while expressing hope that an easing of geopolitical conflicts would allow disinflation to resume. His weekend remarks extended the policy debate after Friday's close.

Equities were less unsettled than Treasuries. The S&P 500 gained 0.17%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.67%, and semiconductor shares advanced 2.78%, even as most S&P constituents declined. The VIX fell to 14.81. Quarterly derivatives expiration helped drive unusually heavy equity turnover. The Dollar Index was unchanged at 100.22, and gold futures gained 0.57% to $4,424.90 an ounce.

## Japan Raises Rates as Asian Policy Pressures Diverge

The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% in a 7-2 vote, but the decision weakened rather than strengthened the yen. Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato, both appointed by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, opposed the increase. Their resistance mattered because the move itself had been almost fully anticipated and traders were looking for a firmer commitment to subsequent tightening.

Governor Kazuo Ueda said policy had entered a stage in which the bank needed to prevent inflation from overshooting 2%, rather than simply establish a durable return to that level. Preemptive action could avoid the need for rapid increases later, he argued. He did not rule out another increase in October or a larger move at some point, but declined to define a terminal rate. The interval of only three months since the previous increase was the shortest between BOJ hikes since 1990.

The yen weakened as much as 1.3% to 158.05 per dollar, while Japanese government bond yields declined slightly across the curve. Wells Fargo's Chidu Narayanan said Ueda's hawkish elements were insufficient to meet market expectations. Daiwa's Kento Minami similarly identified the dissents as the dovish surprise, while regarding the bank's economic and inflation assessment as consistent with a faster pace of tightening. The rate had entered the lower end of the BOJ's estimated neutral range, leaving the interpretation of future restraint particularly important.

The currency subsequently recovered part of its loss after Nikkei reported that the BOJ had asked market participants about exchange-rate levels. At about 1:20 p.m. New York time, the yen was down 0.5% at 156.70. The reported rate check revived intervention expectations; Japan's Finance Ministry could not immediately be reached for comment. It followed the joint U.S.-Japanese support operation earlier in the summer, but did not establish that another purchase of yen had occurred Friday.

Japan's August inflation release explained some of the difficulty in communicating the decision. Consumer prices excluding fresh food rose 1.7% from a year earlier, down from 1.8% and below economists' expectation of no change. Both headline inflation and the measure excluding fresh food and energy were 1.9%. Government support, led by gasoline subsidies, reduced headline inflation by 0.62 percentage point, obscuring some underlying pressure.

The price composition was uneven. Rice fell 15.7%, and processed-food inflation slowed to 2.7% from 3%, while household durables, recreation-related durable goods and medical fees accelerated. Corporate goods prices rose 7.6% from a year earlier, and the number of food and beverage products scheduled for price increases in September was 83% higher than a year before, according to Teikoku Databank. A softer consumer headline therefore arrived alongside substantial pressure earlier in the supply chain.

Australia's central bank was more explicit about the risk of inflation expectations adjusting upward. Governor Michele Bullock told lawmakers Friday that some businesses were beginning to question whether inflation would return below 3%. She stressed that this was a developing concern rather than an explicit, quantified forecast from firms. Persistent Middle East and weather-related shocks, alongside domestic demand, had worsened the trade-off between inflation and employment.

Bullock said some upside inflation risks identified in August were materializing despite slowing growth, and that firms were passing through higher input costs. If those effects became embedded in wages and pricing, a stronger policy response could be necessary. Market-implied odds of an increase at the September meeting rose to roughly 90% from about 84% before her testimony, while 3-year bonds pared earlier gains. The current policy rate is 4.35%.

Sunday's preliminary Cotality housing data supplied a domestic counterweight: the capital-city auction clearance rate fell 4.6 percentage points to 54%. Auction volumes remained more than 30% below a year earlier for a sixth week, even though 1,832 homes went to auction, 16% more than the previous week. Sydney's clearance rate fell to 54%, and Melbourne's to 56%, showing weaker property-market absorption as rate concerns intensified.

China's Friday fiscal figures pointed in another direction. Broad government spending fell 6.7% from a year earlier in August, faster than July's 4.4% decline, while broad revenue rose 2.9%, according to Bloomberg calculations from Finance Ministry data. The monthly deficit shrank by a fifth, leaving an eight-month shortfall of CNY5.5 trillion. The withdrawal of fiscal support added a concrete explanation for weak domestic demand beyond the lending slowdown already evident in earlier releases.

Officials were emphasizing faster use of existing allocations. Policy banks had begun deploying a program capable of unlocking CNY800 billion, mainly for infrastructure in 2026. CICC's Miao Yanliang estimated that planned but unsold government bonds for the remainder of the year equaled around 1.1% of GDP and judged the associated spending sufficient to help meet the 4.5%-5% growth target. Separately on Sunday, the market regulator pledged cost investigations and price inspections aimed at curbing destructive price competition.

Indonesia's new finance minister, Suahasil Nazara, confirmed that roughly IDR299 trillion of government standby funds would remain with state lenders through July 2027. Monthly coordination with banks and the central bank is intended to prevent eventual withdrawals from creating funding gaps. He put the August deficit at 0.93% of GDP and retained the 2.85% full-year target and proposed 2.4% target for 2027. That supplied specific liquidity and fiscal commitments beyond his earlier assurance of adherence to the legal 3% ceiling.

## Europe's Inflation Debate Meets Sovereign Downgrades

France's 10-year yield premium over Germany reached 103 basis points Friday, crossing 1 percentage point for the first time in 14 years. Its 10-year yield traded around 4.50%, and the premium over comparable swaps reached 96 basis points. The underperformance accompanied a broad European bond selloff, but the government's admission that it would miss its deficit target gave French debt a separate fiscal burden.

The government now expects a 2026 deficit of 5.4% of GDP rather than the 5% written into the finance law. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu proposed EUR54 billion of measures to restrain spending and return the shortfall to 5% in 2027. Finance Minister Roland Lescure defended the objective Friday and retained the aim of reaching the EU's 3% limit in 2029. Adoption remains difficult in a fragmented parliament only seven months before presidential elections.

Scope cut France's rating to A+ from AA-, with a stable outlook, while Morningstar DBRS changed the trend on its AA rating to negative. Scope cited repeated fiscal slippage, rising debt and limited reform progress, and expected political fragmentation to persist beyond the election. The ratings actions followed the day's spread widening; they reinforced rather than initiated the warning from the market. ECB President Christine Lagarde said she saw no disorderly market functioning.

France offered further numbers Saturday. Its Budget Ministry projected net primary expenditure growth of 0.7% in 2027, below the European Commission's recommended maximum of 1.2%. Spending would fall to 56.9% of GDP from 57.1%, with tax revenues at 44.2%. Yet debt would rise to 121.7% of GDP in 2027 from 119.3% this year and 115.7% in 2025. Compliance with the proposed spending path would therefore still leave debt climbing. Full proposals are due to reach lawmakers at the end of September, with the Commission's formal assessment in November.

Greece received the opposite ratings verdict. Scope upgraded it to BBB+, its highest score from a major assessor and equal to Scope's rating for Italy. Moody's retained Baa3 but changed the outlook to positive. The agencies pointed to sustained primary surpluses, improved tax administration and a rapidly declining debt ratio. Greece plans to repay about EUR13 billion of bailout debt early in 2026. Scope acknowledged that next spring's election could complicate government formation but considered major policy reversals a limited risk.

After the U.S. fixed-income close Friday, Moody's lowered Poland one notch to A3 and changed its outlook to stable from negative. The agency criticized the persistence of large deficits despite above-trend growth, low unemployment and substantial EU funding. Warsaw's draft budget envisages a deficit of 7.1% of GDP in both 2026 and 2027, with defense, healthcare, social spending and public investment keeping expenditure elevated. Finance Minister Andrzej Domanski promised fiscal strengthening but said it required cooperation from all state institutions, including the president.

Poland also faced a fresh monetary-policy warning. MPC member Wieslaw Janczyk said further tightening could become necessary if oil and gas costs accelerated, taking a more hawkish position than Governor Adam Glapinski's earlier suggestion of a hold until mid-2027. Janczyk regarded the current 3.75% rate as restrictive and positive real rates as disinflationary, but said easing was unrealistic. August inflation was 3.4%, near the top of the 2.5% target's 1-percentage-point tolerance band. His conditional case depended partly on energy prices and government measures to cap fuel costs.

For the ECB, Friday's household survey added evidence of widening expectations. Consumers' one-year inflation forecast rose to 3% in August from 2.9%; the three-year measure increased to 2.9% from 2.7%, and five-year expectations also rose. Respondents continued to expect the economy to contract 1.2% over the coming year. The combination was uncomfortable: higher expected prices without stronger household growth expectations.

Latvian Governor Martins Kazaks said restrictive rates were the likely outcome if economic activity followed the ECB's baseline. Stronger growth would make further increases easier, he argued, and the present 2.5% deposit rate was not a ceiling. Estonia's Ulo Kaasik emphasized prevention: second-round effects had not yet appeared, but avoiding them was the central bank's job.

Lagarde placed greater weight on the full economic response, stressing Friday that energy costs do not mechanically determine interest rates because they also affect growth and consumption. Italian Finance Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti objected that tightening could not by itself resolve a supply-driven inflation shock. A Bloomberg economist survey now envisages a final increase to 2.75% in December, instead of treating September as the endpoint, with rates staying there until December 2027. Market pricing was more aggressive, anticipating at least three further moves.

On Saturday, Greek Governor Yannis Stournaras set out the conditions for choosing between October and December. A September inflation surge or an energy move deep into the ECB's adverse scenario could justify an October increase. Doubt would favor waiting for the next projections; weaker activity would also support a pause. He saw no wage-driven second-round effects so far, but identified fiscal expansion and AI investment as demand pressures alongside repeated supply shocks.

The physical energy news supplied a reason for that vigilance even while futures fell Friday. Saudi Aramco told at least two European refiners that they would receive no crude under long-term contracts in October, extending the delivery problem beyond earlier September delays. Poland's Orlen was seeking alternative suppliers. Dated Brent, the benchmark for physical European barrels, had exceeded $130 during the week. Emmanuel Macron said he would convene the G7 to consider another release of stockpiled oil products.

Weekend reporting added a transport constraint: sending a supertanker cargo from Houston to Asia cost about $26 a barrel, or $52 million a shipment, threatening the economics of long-distance replacement supplies. Saudi Arabia also reported intercepting a missile aimed at Riyadh and thwarting attacks on civilian sites including Yanbu on Saturday. Against that deterioration, U.S. Central Command said the principal Hormuz transit lanes were clear of mines and Gulf allies had shipped more than 1 billion barrels through the strait in recent months. Qatar's prime minister said messages were passing between Washington and Tehran.

Britain's new detail concerned implementation of the BOE's already announced gilt-sale changes. Barclays' Moyeen Islam argued that slower runoff would reduce operational pressure on repo facilities and allow reserves to approach equilibrium more gradually. Six of seven bonds maturing between 2029 and 2034 in the BOE's holdings had 30%-50% of their outstanding stock held there, according to Barclays. With little new supply, individual issues could become scarcer to trade or borrow. The treatment of bonds transferred to the Debt Management Office still required clarification.

## Financing Remains Available, but at a Higher Price

CleanSpark completed its Meta-linked data-center financing on substantially stronger demand than at launch. The five-year junk bonds priced at 98.5 cents to yield 8.25%, compared with initial discussion around 8.5%. The offering grew to almost $2.28 billion and attracted about $10 billion of orders, more than four times its size. The yield still exceeded the average for BB debt by roughly 1.75 percentage points.

The final terms resolved a concrete primary-market test for a construction-stage project supported by Meta's guarantee of rent and operating expenses under a 20-year lease. Investors accepted a lower yield than initially discussed, but the borrowing cost remained materially above the below-6% yields achieved by some comparable investment-grade-tenant financings earlier in the year. CoreWeave also completed its $3 billion convertible sale, though it had to offer a higher coupon and lower conversion premium to attract buyers.

SoftBank disclosed a much larger collection of financing developments through people familiar with its arrangements. It increased the Arm-backed margin-loan facility by $5 billion to $25 billion and added $450 million to a separate credit line, taking that facility to $6.5 billion. It also secured an $11.87 billion loan for its OpenAI investment. Apollo was in talks to increase another loan by $3.6 billion to $9 billion. Together, the committed and possible additions totaled $20.92 billion.

The Arm facility retained a margin of about 225 basis points over SOFR plus a 25-basis-point credit adjustment spread. Lenders offered about $7 billion against a requested increase of $3 billion-$5 billion, helped by Arm's 142% share-price rise this year. As of May, collateral comprised 769 million Arm shares, representing 72% of the chipmaker. The separate $6.5 billion line involved more than 20 banks and carried a 210-basis-point margin over SOFR. Those margins sit above the floating benchmark rather than fixing SoftBank's total interest cost.

SoftBank also repaid the full $25.9 billion outstanding on a one-year OpenAI financing this week as it replaced short-term borrowing with longer maturities. Its financing activity supports a $65 billion OpenAI commitment. People familiar with investor discussions said it was considering a $10 billion-$20 billion bond sale; SoftBank said its New York meetings were non-deal updates and that no issuance decision had been made. Its CDS had reached a three-year high earlier in the week despite lenders' appetite for the collateral-backed facilities.

Other borrowers were developing different routes to market. JPMorgan, Santander and NatWest arranged GBP1.1 billion of bridge funding for Drax's acquisition of Bluefield Solar Income Fund. The banks intend to distribute the debt to institutions later this year or early in 2027, potentially alongside refinancing of Drax's existing obligations. The acquisition adds solar and wind assets to a business repositioning itself toward flexible power and storage.

The Korea-US Strategic Investment Corporation sent requests for proposals for a possible debut dollar bond of as much as $2 billion. The entity implements South Korea's $350 billion U.S. investment pledge and could appoint arrangers by the end of September for issuance early next year. Financing discussions remain preliminary, and the government said the first investment project had not been finalized despite media reports identifying a Texas gas-fired power plant.

New research quantified the shortening of corporate liabilities without requiring another round of issuer anecdotes. Barclays reported Friday that average maturity in the U.S. high-grade market had fallen to 10.3 years from a peak of 12.4. In Europe, about 80% of this year's issuance matures within a decade, compared with 65% last year. Asia-Pacific companies sold only one noncallable dollar bond of at least 10 years in the first half of September, a $500 million Norinchukin issue, against roughly $6.7 billion of such issuance in the comparable 2025 period.

The shift reduces the time borrowers commit to today's interest costs but brings refinancing forward. It also leaves insurers and pension funds with fewer long assets outside the heavy AI-related issuance. Primary access was still broad: U.S. investment-grade sales totaled about $54 billion for the week, and Europe had its busiest Friday for debt sales since April.

Fund flows were less comfortable. LSEG Lipper figures showed global bond-fund net purchases slowing to $554 million, the weakest weekly inflow in five months. Short-to-intermediate government and Treasury funds attracted $3.49 billion for an eleventh consecutive weekly inflow, while comparable investment-grade funds lost $817 million. The appetite for government exposure was not matched uniformly across credit and tax-exempt debt.

Municipal funds lost about $1.8 billion in the week ended Wednesday, their largest withdrawal since April 2025 and the end of a 21-week inflow streak. Open-end funds drove much of the exodus, with ETFs also losing money. Municipal returns were down roughly 1.7% for the year, and bonds offered for bidding had risen to about $2.5 billion, also the most since April 2025. Ten-year municipal yields stood around 74% of comparable Treasuries on Wednesday. Hennion & Walsh's James Pruskowski warned that such redemption cycles rarely end after a single week.

At Friday's close, U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed and hard-currency emerging-market spreads were noticeably tighter. Higher Treasury yields still weighed on returns: LQD lost 0.44%, HYG 0.24%, and EMB 0.30% on a distribution-adjusted basis.

## Asset Sales and Refinancing Divide Credit Outcomes

Shapoorji Pallonji Group's lenders faced a contrast between improved asset-value expectations and an immediate cash requirement. The group was seeking a three- to six-month extension of INR35 billion, about $365 million, due September 30 on Porteast Investment's zero-coupon bond. Funds raised in July that had been intended to service the obligation were being held for other purposes, according to people familiar with the talks. Creditors would receive a consent fee, with terms still under discussion in meetings arranged by Deutsche Bank.

Meanwhile, SP Group's $650 million Mercury Finance dollar notes, carrying a 14.5% coupon, gained 1.8 cents during the week to a record 101.9 cents. Investors were responding to Tata Sons' decision to pursue a listing, which could unlock value from SP's 18.4% stake. Some Eqyizen rupee bonds were being offered at an 18.75% yield, compared with 18.95% at July issuance, and some distributors reduced minimum tickets to INR10 million from INR100 million.

The asset's prospective liquidity did not eliminate the need for Porteast's extension. Its $3.4 billion zero-coupon financing raised last year at a 19.75% annual yield is backed by the Tata stake; a waiver increasing its loan-to-value limit from 34% to 40% had already been extended through September 30. Over the weekend, Tata Trusts disputed the legal validity of the resolution reappointing N. Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman. The parties hired lawyers for a potentially prolonged battle, adding a governance complication to investors' hopes of monetizing the holding.

Brazilian steelmaker CSN offered more tangible progress toward asset disposals. Huaxin, Votorantim and Polimix submitted binding bids of about BRL11 billion each for its cement business, below the BRL15 billion sought, according to people familiar with the negotiations. The company might accept the lower price. The unit secures a loan of at least $1.2 billion, making the handling of pledged assets important to the deleveraging proceeds.

CSN was also selling Germany's Stahlwerk Thuringen and considering separate sales of infrastructure assets rather than a combined minority stake. Its bonds had returned about 5% since Fabio Schvartsman's September 2 appointment as chief executive, against a 0.5% decline in a broader EM corporate gauge. The rally still left them down about 11.2% this year. Net debt stood at BRL42.1 billion at June 30, or 3.5 times EBITDA, after a tenth consecutive quarterly net loss. Asset-sale execution, rather than the management change alone, now determines how much of the balance-sheet pressure can ease.

European property debt showed the opposite funding outcome. Net Zero Properties abandoned a EUR500 million bond despite offering an issue discount and increased coupon. Its June interest-cover ratio was 1.3 times, close to its medium-term policy minimum of 1.2. Part of the proceeds would have refinanced more expensive Castlelake mezzanine debt, but investors questioned cash generation after interest and the valuation of the property portfolio.

NZP said the book was fully covered and that market volatility had pushed pricing above cheaper alternatives; it described itself as well funded for acquisitions. The cancellation occurred as property became the weakest European high-yield sector for the month, returning minus 2.03% against minus 0.9% for the broader index. Vivion's hybrid carrying an 8.125% coupon traded near 85 cents. Higher financing costs are pressing on debt service and property valuations simultaneously, while rents adjust more slowly.

A separate weekend investigation identified another risk in European property lending. Banks said privacy restrictions impeded access to borrowers' insurance and building-condition data just as regulators increased scrutiny of fire, flood and drought exposures. The ECB highlighted the mismatch between annually renewable insurance and loans that can run for 30 years. UniCredit had added EUR100 million of climate-related provisions. The issue is whether coverage that protects collateral at origination remains affordable and available over the life of the loan.

In sovereign credit, Moody's cut Mozambique to Caa3 in a late-Friday announcement, warning that domestic financing strain had spread to external obligations. The country remained current on its $900 million 2031 eurobond, but the agency's rating was consistent with a restructuring involving investor losses of 20%-35%. External arrears had reached $328 million at end-2025. The downgrade challenged the optimism behind a recovery in the bond to 94.88 cents, nearly 30% above April lows.

An IMF mission ended Friday with the fund reporting subdued activity but signs of recovery. Mozambique's government said a November visit could lead to a staff-level agreement. The combination leaves program negotiations and debt treatment unresolved even as major LNG projects advance; Moody's loss range describes its restructuring assessment, not agreed creditor terms.

Pakistan reported a funding improvement instead. The prime minister's office put foreign-exchange reserves at a record $21.4 billion after Eurobond proceeds arrived, citing stronger remittances, services exports and the current account. The new receipt strengthened the external buffer, although exposure to imported energy remained a vulnerability. The country's recent issuance has expanded financing options while an IMF visit is expected in the coming week.

Across emerging markets, fresh allocation evidence showed investors favoring local bonds over dollar debt. A September 4-9 Bank of America survey of 38 managers overseeing $444 billion found 84% overweight local relative to hard-currency debt, up from 38% in August. Local sovereign bonds had outperformed dollar bonds by more than 3 percentage points since June's end. September withdrawals from the largest dollar-debt ETF exceeded $800 million, while the largest local-currency ETF attracted about $41 million.

The dollar remained a constraint on that preference. Its broad advance last week came as local EM bond returns were increasingly negatively correlated with the currency. Robeco's Diliana Deltcheva saw more opportunities in local markets and limited additional spread compression in dollar bonds, while Jupiter's Harry Richards warned that higher Treasury yields would particularly challenge weaker issuers' refinancing capacity. The strong relative performance of local debt therefore rested on country-level inflation and currency outcomes as well as starting yields.

## Forward Market Significance

The September 22 sale of $69 billion of 2-year Treasuries and September 23 sale of $70 billion of 5-year notes will test demand in the maturities leading the selloff. A 7-year auction follows September 24. Gross Treasury auctions next week total more than $700 billion, according to Mischler's Tony Farren, alongside dealer expectations of roughly $40 billion of U.S. high-grade corporate issuance. Sysco could bring a $17 billion financing, including 30- and 40-year notes, for its Jetro Restaurant Depot acquisition; SoftBank's possible offering would add a separate large call on capital.

The growth test has sharpened after manufacturing's contraction. September 22 brings ADP's weekly employment estimate and the Richmond Fed survey, followed by S&P Global's September flash PMIs on September 23. Consensus anticipates manufacturing at 53.6 after 53.9 and services at 56 after 56.5. Jobless claims on September 24 and durable-goods and capital-goods figures on September 25 will help establish whether August's weaker production is spreading to hiring and investment. Friday's final University of Michigan survey also brings updated inflation expectations.

Fed communication will address a market anticipating substantially more tightening than the median policymaker. Austan Goolsbee speaks Monday, with John Williams and Philip Jefferson among Tuesday's speakers; Beth Hammack speaks Thursday. The consequential distinction is whether officials treat weaker factory output as emerging restraint or continue to emphasize broad inflation and resilient demand, as Schmid and Kashkari have done.

The September 24 Trump-Xi summit now follows trade talks begun in New York by Scott Bessent and He Lifeng. An extension of the truce due to expire in November, tariffs, investment and AI are on the agenda. The duration and terms of any extension matter more than the earlier postponement of a U.S. tariff announcement, because they determine how much renewed trade-cost uncertainty remains after the meeting.

Japan's holiday through Wednesday raises the risk of sharp currency moves after Friday's reported rate check. Thin liquidity could magnify either renewed yen weakness or official action. Energy markets face a distinct delivery test after October's canceled Saudi allocations: alternative supply, shipping costs and security around Red Sea infrastructure will determine whether lower futures prices bring meaningful relief to refiners.

India is expected to finalize its October-March borrowing calendar on September 25. Planned gross issuance for that period is INR7.96 trillion, including INR65 billion not raised in the failed September 11 three-year auction. Market participants favor more three- and five-year supply, but RBI liquidity-draining bond sales are already pressing on shorter rates. JPMorgan's Jahangir Aziz separately warned Friday that markets might overestimate the tightening sustainable after earlier stimulus fades, despite anticipating an initial quarter-point increase. The maturity mix will therefore meet an unsettled policy outlook.

Australia's Thursday employment figures will inform the following week's RBA decision after Bullock's warning and weaker housing auctions. Europe's flash business surveys will test the resilience underlying the ECB's tightening case. France's end-September budget submission and SP Group's September 30 payment deadline are more immediate credit-specific milestones: one tests political capacity to deliver fiscal restraint, the other whether prospective asset value can bridge a current funding need.

section_summaries.summary: The distinction was between confidence that central banks would act and uncertainty over how far they would go. U.S. real yields rose without an increase in long-term inflation compensation, Japan's expected hike disappointed currency markets, and France's sovereign premium widened. Financing remained available, but dependable funding access increasingly separated borrowers from those relying on asset sales or payment extensions.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries surrender their relief rally as expectations of further Fed tightening persist
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries reversed Thursday's rally, with the 2-year yield rising 9 basis points to 4.76% and the 10-year climbing 7 basis points to 5.01%. Investors anticipated further Fed increases despite August manufacturing output falling 0.3% against expectations for a 0.3% rise. Jeff Schmid emphasized inflation across goods and services rather than oil alone. Real yields rose while long-term inflation compensation held steady, locating the immediate adjustment in real borrowing costs. Higher European yields and prospective debt supply added pressure.

Japan raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, but a divided vote and inconclusive guidance weakened the yen; a reported exchange-rate check later reversed part of its decline. France's 10-year premium over Germany reached 103 basis points as the government acknowledged a larger deficit, alongside rising European household inflation expectations.

Credit remained accessible but increasingly differentiated. CleanSpark expanded its Meta-linked financing to almost $2.28 billion at an 8.25% yield, while SoftBank secured substantial additional borrowing and replaced short-term debt with longer maturities. That access contrasted with SP Group's request for a payment extension and Net Zero Properties' abandoned bond sale. Upcoming Treasury auctions will test demand in the maturities leading the selloff, while activity releases and Fed commentary will clarify how much further restraint officials consider necessary.
overall_summary.summary: Weaker factory output and falling oil failed to ease pressure on bonds as inflation concerns extended beyond energy, while large financings remained possible on terms that increasingly distinguished borrowers' funding strength.
